How extension works

Within each four-row family, the generator identifies the fixed operator structure and the arithmetic growth of every repeated a-block. It then extends those block lengths, calculates the resulting target, and accepts the new row only when the identity remains exact for all nine possible digits.

Source status: the first four rows are marked “author’s row”; later rows are marked “generated extension.” Duplicate families and rows containing transcription or identity errors are excluded.

Individual fallback: if no pattern family contains the requested target, the generator checks the author’s running-type or fraction-type collection and then the structural single-value constructor. An isolated identity is labelled as an individual representation and is never presented as a pattern.
